events.title: Supreme Court reverses Fourth Circuit decision in Klein v. Martin
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the State's petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Klein v. Martin, reversing the Fourth Circuit's decision that had affirmed the award of a new trial for Charles Brandon Martin. The Fourth Circuit had ruled that the state court failed to apply the correct legal standard under the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act (AEDPA) regarding the materiality of undisclosed evidence. The Supreme Court found that the state appellate court had applied the correct standard and that a fairminded jurist could conclude that the undisclosed forensic report was not material to the outcome of Martin's trial.
events.why_relevant: This decision underscores the Supreme Court's interpretation of AEDPA standards, affecting federal habeas corpus review of state court decisions.

events.title: Supreme Court releases opinion in Klein v. Martin (25-51)
events.summary: The Supreme Court released an official slip opinion in Klein v. Martin. Docket number(s): 25-51.
events.why_relevant: The Supreme Court's official opinion in Klein v. Martin is a primary legal source. Supreme Court opinions can define binding national law and alter the legal position of the executive branch, federal agencies, states, litigants, and democratic institutions.

events.title: Certiorari Denied in Thompson v. Texas
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the application for a stay of execution and the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Charles Thompson v. Texas. The application was initially presented to Justice Alito, who referred it to the full Court. The denial means that the execution of the death sentence will proceed as scheduled, and the Court will not review the case.
events.why_relevant: The denial of certiorari and stay of execution affects the administration of justice and the finality of capital punishment cases.
